blocks.md: Every app you have ever used — a to-do list, a habit tracker, a social feed — is mostly the same four operations playing on repeat: **Create, Read, Update, Delete**. Master CRUD and you can build the data layer of almost anything. Today you will wire those four operations directly from React into your Supabase database using the JavaScript client.

blocks.canDo: create, read, update and delete data from React
blocks.md: By the end of this session you will be able to use the Supabase JavaScript client to query a table, insert a new row, update an existing row, and delete a row — and handle loading and error states for each operation.

**CRUD = Create · Read · Update · Delete** — the four verbs of persistent data.

With the Supabase JavaScript client, every operation starts the same way:

```js
supabase.from('habits')   // pick the table
```

Then chain the right verb:

| Goal | Chain |
|------|-------|
| Read all rows | `.select()` |
| Insert a row | `.insert({ name: 'Exercise' })` |
| Update a row | `.update({ done: true }).eq('id', 7)` |
| Delete a row | `.delete().eq('id', 7)` |

Every call returns a Promise with `{ data, error }`. Always check both: show a spinner while the call is in flight (`loading` state) and show a message if `error` is set. Skipping these two states is the most common mistake beginners make.

Work through the official Supabase React Quickstart. It walks you through creating a project, adding the client library, and running your first `select()` — the read foundation for everything else in this session.
blocks.label: Supabase React Quickstart — read (select)

blocks.md: The quickstart only shows `.select()`. Use these three short Supabase JS reference pages — one per write operation — to learn the exact call signatures for insert, update, and delete. Read all three before you write any write-side code.
blocks.label: create / update / delete — Supabase JS Reference

blocks.md: **Always use `.eq('id', row.id)` when updating or deleting.** Without a filter, Supabase will apply the change to *every* row in the table. The `.eq()` method is your WHERE clause — treat it as required, not optional.

questions.question: What does CRUD stand for?
questions.explanation: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, Delete — the four fundamental data operations almost every app is built on.

questions.question: In the Supabase JS client, what does `.from('habits')` do?
options: It creates a new table called 'habits'
It selects and returns all rows from the habits table immediately
It sets the target table for the query — you chain .select(), .insert(), .update(), or .delete() after it
It deletes the habits table from the database
questions.explanation: `.from('habits')` picks the table you want to work with; it does not execute anything on its own — you must chain a verb like `.select()` or `.insert()` next.

questions.question: Why should you always manage loading and error states when making Supabase calls?
options: Supabase throws an exception if you don't, crashing the app
It prevents the component from re-rendering
Network calls are async and can fail — without these states users see broken UIs or stale data with no feedback
It is only needed when using .delete(), not .select()
questions.explanation: Database calls are asynchronous and can fail due to network issues or permission errors. A loading state gives users feedback while they wait; an error state lets you show a useful message instead of a blank screen.

blocks.md:
**What you covered:**

- CRUD stands for **Create, Read, Update, Delete** — the backbone of almost every app
- Use `supabase.from('tableName')` to target a table, then chain `.select()`, `.insert()`, `.update().eq()`, or `.delete().eq()`
- Every call returns `{ data, error }` — always handle both
- Show a loading state while the call is in flight; show an error message if something goes wrong

**Up next:** Authentication — controlling who can read and write your data.
